describe: make a whole game where you dodge or avoid things
guide: A new thing needs three pieces in three places, and with only two it does nothing: create it once ABOVE the game loop, move it INSIDE the loop, and draw it inside the loop AFTER screen.fill(...). Give its speed, size and colour named constants at the top.

For a dodging game, make several things that drift across the screen and come back round, and check for a touch every frame -- acting only in the frame a touch begins (scene.touched(player, things) in a game with a scene), so a thing crossing the start cannot hold the player there.
guide_scene: Build it with game_object, one call for each thing: the player's look (name player -- a picture they added, or a drawing), the things to dodge (a drawing, or a picture they added, with count, moves: left and touch: avoid), and a sky or a road if they want a scene. Open Nest draws and moves each one every frame.
Only what game_object has no word for -- a score that counts dodges, lives, a game over -- is edit_file.
report: I added $what. $touch Move with the arrow keys and keep out of their way. $ship
Here's a start: $what. $touch Dodge them with the arrow keys. $ship
I made it a dodging game: $what. $touch $ship
teach: The things are made once above the loop and moved every frame inside it, the scene draws them, and a collision check sends you back when one hits.
_note: needs_words: a whole game is only built when the child asks for a game. Measured (SPIKES.md section 25N): as one part of a longer message, 'add some walls i have to get around' was read as this recipe at 1.00. not_words: a whole game of another kind is not this one. Measured on the game builds (SPIKES.md section 33): on Gary Fast, Open Nest's own Platform Game idea card -- 'Make a platform game' -- was built as the dodging game at once, five asteroids falling on a platformer. None of the three labelled whole-game requests names one of these words.
